runbook: R-18 / R-19 (fresh independent oracle; evidence tree = `git archive HEAD data docs/math-foundations.md` only)

step_1_stack_value.claim: Carve at full stacks reduces the target's armor by 30%.
step_1_stack_value.work: Cached wiki text for item 3071 passive 'Carve': 6% armor reduction per stack, stacking up to 5 times. 5 x 0.06 = 0.30.

step_2_who_it_applies_to.claim: Carve is a reduction of the TARGET's armor stat, so every attacker hitting that target sees the reduced armor — including an ally support who does not own the item.
work: data/items.json[3071].simpleDescription: 'Dealing physical damage to enemy champions reduces their Armor' — the effect writes the target's Armor stat, it is not an attacker-side penetration.

docs/math-foundations.md §2.2/§2.3 keeps the two halves separate on exactly this basis: penetration is attacker-side and floors at 0, while 'Only armor/magic *reduction* effects can push resistance negative' — i.e. reduction mutates the target's resistance value itself.

The roster's support carries Bloodsong, whose Spellblade proc deals '100% base AD bonus physical damage' (data/items.json[3877]) — physical damage, so the target's armor is on the support's damage path and a 30% armor reduction is load-bearing for the support's numbers.
step_2_who_it_applies_to.result: An armor_reduction_percent entry sourced to the ally's Black Cleaver legitimately belongs in the support's resistance-reduction view of the shared target.

step_3_factor_cross_check.claim: The old leaf's `factor` is exactly the damage amplification implied by its own `fraction` under the engine's documented resistance identity — the two fields are mutually consistent, which an artifact/garbage entry would not be.
work: Sanity of the fit: amp(100)=1.17647, amp(110)=1.18644, amp(125)=1.20000, amp(150)=1.21951 — 1.2 is hit only at R = 125, a round scenario-grade armor value; 125 → 87.5 armor after the 30% shred.
step_3_factor_cross_check.result: factor = 1.2 is the exact, self-consistent consequence of fraction = 0.3 against 125 armor.

step_4_timing.claim: 5 stacks being up at event index 46 is consistent with the source text.
step_4_timing.work: Carve stacks last 6 seconds and refresh on every instance of physical damage to that champion; math-foundations §2.3(2) notes the stack duration '(6 s) is always longer than the engine's inter-swing interval for any realistic AS·u > 1/6, so expiry does not rescue the constant'. 46 events into a Black-Cleaver-holder's fight, the cap is held.
step_4_timing.result: Full-stack (0.3) is the expected steady-state value at this point in the timeline.

independent_computation.conclusion: Every field of the old leaf reproduces from cached source text plus the documented resistance identity: 5 x 6% = 30% armor reduction, target-side, therefore visible to the ally support, amplifying that support's physical damage by exactly 1.2x against 125 armor. Deleting the leaf removes a real, sourced game effect from the support's view and (if the factor is load-bearing) understates the support's physical damage by a factor of 1.2.

sources_quoted.locator: id 3071 — Black Cleaver, passives[0] 'Carve' (unique: true), branches[0]
sources_quoted.quote: Dealing {{as|physical damage}} to an enemy champion applies a stack of ''Carve'' for 6 seconds, stacking up to 5 times. Each stack inflicts {{as|6% armor reduction}}, up to {{as|30%|armor}} at 5 stacks.
Dealing physical damage to enemy champions reduces their Armor

After using an ability, your next basic attack within 10 seconds deals {{as|100% '''base''' AD}} {{as|'''bonus''' physical damage}} [[on-hit]]. If the target is a champion, inflict them with ''Expose Weakness'' for 4 seconds, causing them to take {{rd|8%|5%}} increased damage from all sources ({{fd|1.5}} second cooldown, starts after using the empowered attack).
Only armor/magic *reduction* effects can push resistance negative; penetration floors at 0 (Section 2.2).

The stack *duration* (6 s) is always longer than the engine's inter-swing interval for any realistic AS·u > 1/6, so expiry does not rescue the constant — this is a documented tuning constant, not a theorem.

considered_and_rejected.hypothesis: Percentage armor reduction was correctly suppressed because the target's armor had already gone negative (docs/math-foundations.md §2.3(3): 'percentage armor reduction cannot' reduce armor below 0).
considered_and_rejected.rejected_because: The leaf's own factor is 1.2 > 1 against R = 125 > 0 — the armor at that step is solidly positive, so the negative-armor guard cannot be what fires here.

considered_and_rejected.hypothesis: The support deals magic damage, so an armor entry is irrelevant.
considered_and_rejected.rejected_because: The roster's support item is Bloodsong, whose Spellblade proc is explicitly '''bonus''' physical damage; armor is on the support's damage path.

considered_and_rejected.hypothesis: The support does not own Black Cleaver, so attributing Carve to the support is a mis-attribution.
considered_and_rejected.rejected_because: Carve reduces the TARGET's Armor stat ('reduces their Armor'), not the holder's penetration. A reduced target armor stat is a single shared number seen by every attacker on that target; excluding ally-sourced reduction from an ally's view would be the error, not the fix.

residual_uncertainty.scope_of_this_oracle: Per runbook, only data/ and docs/math-foundations.md were read. src/, tests/, scripts/golden_baseline.json, the diff, the plan and git history were NOT read, so the sibling entries support_resistance_reduction[0..6] are unknown to me.
residual_uncertainty.the_one_scenario_that_would_flip_this: If one of entries [0..6] is itself an identical 'Black Cleaver — Carve' armor_reduction_percent entry, then removing [7] is a correct de-duplication: data/items.json marks Carve "unique": true, and a unique target debuff does not stack with a second copy of itself (0.7 x 0.7 = 0.49 armor would be a double-shred bug). Absent visibility of the siblings I cannot confirm or exclude that, and I flag it as the sole path by which 'absent' could be right.
residual_uncertainty.confidence: moderate-high on the value itself (0.3 / 1.2 are exactly reproducible from source), moderate on the presence/absence question.
